nodes.label: Wall View Layout
nodes.rationale: Side-by-side vertical columns, one per agent, each streaming that agent's live tool-call transcript. Lets a single operator watch an entire multi-agent team at once instead of switching between sessions; active agent columns are bright while departed agents are dimmed to push attention toward live work.

nodes.label: View Modes (wall / overview / tasks / rail / grid)
nodes.rationale: Five alternative projections of the same team session, suggesting the console separates session data from presentation so the operator can choose density vs. detail.

nodes.label: team-lead Agent
nodes.rationale: Orchestrator agent on claude-opus-5, status 'working', 68% context used (680k/1M), ~$94.52 api-equiv. Runs on the larger model and accounts for nearly all session cost, implying a design where an expensive lead delegates implementation to cheaper sonnet workers.

nodes.label: impl-task-1 Agent
nodes.rationale: Worker agent on claude-sonnet-5, status 'departed' after completing 'Implement Task 1 scaffo...'; transcript shows edit/test/commit loop ending in a SendMessage status report and an approved shutdown_request.

nodes.label: impl-task-2 Agent
nodes.rationale: Worker agent on claude-sonnet-5, status 'departed' after 'Implement Task 2 catalog'; transcript shows tests (14/14 passing), a git commit, and a SendMessage 'STATUS: DONE commit SHA' report back to the team lead.

nodes.label: Live Tool-Call Transcript Stream
nodes.rationale: Each column renders a condensed feed of tool invocations (Bash, Read, Edit, Write, ToolSearch, WebFetch, SendMessage) with truncated one-line results, glyph-coded (bullet for calls, corner for results, x for errors, check for successes). Optimized for scanning activity at a glance rather than reading full output.

nodes.label: Token and Cost Tracking
nodes.source_location: top bar and each column header
nodes.rationale: Every agent header shows a context-usage progress bar, percent, tokens/limit (e.g. 680k/1M), and an api-equivalent dollar figure; the top bar aggregates the team (149.0M tokens, ~$97.77, 1h 14m). Makes spend and context pressure first-class monitoring signals per agent and for the whole session.

nodes.label: NEEDS YOU Attention Bar
nodes.rationale: A dedicated queue ('NEEDS YOU · 0 nothing waiting') for items blocked on human input, so the operator does not have to scan every column to find agents waiting on them.

nodes.label: Panel Bar Keyboard Controls
nodes.rationale: Terminal-style keyboard-first control surface: select, open, esc interrupt, x stop, ^T tasks, plus current selection ('team-lead 68%', '7 departed'). The console behaves like a TUI-in-the-browser aimed at fast operator intervention.

nodes.label: Per-Agent Message Input
nodes.rationale: Each column has its own prompt ('message team-lead', 'message impl-task-1'), letting the operator steer any individual agent directly without going through the lead.

nodes.label: Agent Lifecycle States (working / departed)
nodes.rationale: Agents are labeled 'working' or 'departed'; the panel bar counts 7 departed. Finished workers stay visible on the wall (dimmed, transcript preserved) rather than disappearing, keeping an audit trail of completed work.

nodes.label: SendMessage Team Coordination
nodes.rationale: Workers report completion to the team lead via SendMessage ('STATUS: DONE commit SHA...', 'Message sent to team-lead') and request shutdown via a shutdown_request that the lead approves ('Shutdown approved'). Coordination and lifecycle transitions are message-driven rather than implicit.
